Founder Voting Structure
We believe that our seven co-founders, Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei, Tom Brown, Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan,
Sam McCandlish, and Christopher Olah, as a group, are distinctly equipped to be stewards of our mission. Our
co-founders have been instrumental in building our leadership position and establishing the mission-driven
values that define our company. In addition, Dr. Amodei serves as our Chief Executive Officer and a member of
our board of directors and Ms. Amodei serves as our President and Chairperson of our board of directors. Their
long-term strategic vision has been critical to our success and will continue to guide our future. In our highly
competitive industry, success requires visionary leadership, strong direction, and the kind of decisiveness
necessary to make bold investments, pursue transformative opportunities, and compete effectively against
formidable competitors, while also balancing the pecuniary interests of our stockholders with the Company
Purpose and the best interests of those materially affected by our conduct.
We believe that our success depends in part on establishing a capital structure that enables our co-founders,
management, and board of directors to focus on strategic initiatives that create lasting value for our
stakeholders, rather than facing pressure to prioritize short-term results or purely pecuniary objectives at the
expense of our long-term vision and mission. Immediately prior to the completion of this offering, we will issue
a single share of Class F common stock, a special class of our common stock, to the Founder LLC, a limited
liability company of which our seven co-founders will initially be the sole members and that will be managed by
its members. Our Class F common stock will be entitled to an aggregate number of votes that equals 50.1% of
the total voting power of our outstanding shares of capital stock as of the applicable record date with respect to
matters submitted to stockholders generally, including the election of our directors other than the Class T
directors.
Our Class F common stock will be voted by the Founder LLC in a manner determined in accordance with the
Founder LLC Agreement. Generally, the Founder LLC will vote as determined by a majority of the members of
the Founder LLC entitled to vote thereunder. Our seven co-founders will initially be the sole members. Upon
the incapacity or death of any of our co-founders, a successor member may be admitted to the Founder LLC
until the tenth anniversary of the completion of this offering. We refer to our seven co-founders and any
successors in the Founder LLC as “Continuing Founders.”
When there have been fewer than three Continuing Founders (not including any successor member who is a
“Non-Qualifying Member” as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement) for 90 consecutive calendar days, a 450-
day transition period will commence (the “Class F Transition Period”). Upon completion of the Class F
Transition Period, all of our Class F common stock and Class E common stock then issued and outstanding will
be redeemed by us for no consideration and certain other governance changes will take effect.
Regardless of the length of time that has elapsed since the completion of this offering or the circumstances that
resulted in the removal of a Continuing Founder, one or more successor members may be admitted to the
Founder LLC during the Class F Transition Period as needed to ensure that there are three Continuing
Founders serving until completion of the Class F Transition Period. The admission of any successor member
during the Class F Transition Period will not cure the event that commenced the Class F Transition Period or
extend the Class F Transition Period. For additional information, see the section titled “Description of Capital
Stock.”
A Continuing Founder will be removed from the Founder LLC upon the earliest to occur of (i) such Continuing
Founder’s resignation as a member of the Founder LLC; (ii) such Continuing Founder’s death or incapacity; (iii)
with respect to each of our seven original co-founders, such original co-founder’s ceasing to hold (together with
such original co-founder’s related holders) on any record date for a vote of our stockholders a number of shares

vote our Class F common stock.
The voting power of our Class F common stock will not be impacted by future issuances of our capital stock that
may cause economic or voting dilution to stockholders, such as issuances for capital raising purposes,
acquisitions, or employee compensation. This structure will allow the Founder LLC to determine the outcome
of matters submitted to a vote of our stockholders generally, including the election of those directors not elected
by the LTBT, certain amendments to our organizational documents, and the approval by our stockholders of
any merger, consolidation, sale of substantially all our assets, or other major corporate transaction requiring
stockholder approval.

Philanthropy
We founded Anthropic on the belief that the most transformative technology in human history demands an
extraordinary level of responsibility, and that responsibility extends far beyond building safe systems. We
intend to direct a meaningful portion of our resources toward ensuring that frontier AI is safe and its benefits
are broadly distributed, which we refer to as our public benefit initiatives. These initiatives include the Initial
Public Benefit Issuance and the future Public Benefit Issuances. In addition, our co-founders have each pledged
to dedicate 80% of their personal equity in Anthropic to philanthropic causes. For additional information
regarding these pledges, including related risks, see the section titled “Risk Factors—Risks Related to
Ownership of our Class A Common Stock.” Separate from the co-founders’ pledges, we also maintain a donation
matching program through which employees can pledge a meaningful portion of their equity awards toward
charitable giving, which we match with shares of our Class N common stock. Further, certain donor-advised
funds may from time to time receive donations of shares directly from us or from one or more of our
stockholders, and we are party to certain irrevocable proxy agreements with such donor-advised funds, as
described under “Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions—Irrevocable Proxy Agreements.”

common stock or to redeem our Class T common stock.

Board Governance
Decisions regarding our business and affairs are made by our board of directors.
Immediately prior to the
completion of this offering, we will enter into the Stockholders’ Agreement with the LTBT and the Founder
LLC, under which they will agree to vote their shares and take other actions to give effect to the board
composition, director nomination, and director removal provisions described in our governing documents.
Collectively, the LTBT and the Founder LLC will have the ability to elect all members of our board of directors.
Regardless of the class or classes of stock by which a director is elected, there is no limit to the number of terms
a director may serve.
While the LTBT has significant influence over our board of directors through its ability to generally elect and
remove a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors, neither the LTBT nor the Trustees have
decision-making authority in the day-to-day management or strategy setting of the company. The LTBT’s role is
to select directors who are well-equipped to make decisions in furtherance of the responsible balancing of the
pecuniary interests of our stockholders, the best interests of those materially affected by our conduct, and the
Company Purpose, and to support our management’s decision-making through advice and guidance. The
Trustees aim to choose directors who have the necessary business skills, experience, and expertise to oversee
the management of our business effectively and in a manner that responsibly balances (i) the pecuniary
interests of our stockholders, (ii) the best interests of those materially affected by our conduct, and (iii) the
Company Purpose.
The Founder LLC will also have significant influence over our business and affairs through its ability to vote our
Class F common stock, which is entitled to an aggregate number of votes that equals 50.1% of the total voting
power of our outstanding shares of capital stock as of the applicable record date with respect to matters
submitted to stockholders generally. The Founder LLC will be able to elect and remove the directors who are
not Class T directors and determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of our stockholders generally
251

(including the approval of any merger, sale of our company, or other significant corporate transaction requiring
stockholder approval) for the foreseeable future.
We are considered a “controlled company” within the meaning of the Nasdaq Global Select Market corporate
governance requirements because the LTBT, as the sole holder of our Class T common stock, generally has the
power to elect a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors. As such, we are permitted to opt
out of compliance with certain Nasdaq Global Select Market corporate governance requirements. Accordingly, if
we elect not to comply with certain requirements, you will not have the same protections afforded to
stockholders of companies that are subject to all of the Nasdaq Global Select Market corporate governance
requirements. Although we qualify as a “controlled company,” we do not expect to rely on this exemption except
with respect to our NGC, which will not consist entirely of independent directors. Our board of directors
currently consists of a majority of independent directors and our audit and compensation committees currently
consist entirely of independent directors.

Director Terms
Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that will become effective immediately prior to the
completion of this offering will provide that prior to the Class F Sunset Time, we will not have a classified board
of directors, and all directors will be elected for annual terms. Each director’s term will continue until the next
annual meeting and until the election and qualification of their successor, or their earlier death, resignation, or
removal.
Following the Class F Sunset Time, our board of directors will shift to having a classified board of directors
consisting of three classes of approximately equal size, each serving staggered three-year terms. At such time,
257
Table of Contents
each of our directors would be assigned by the then-current board of directors to a class. If
our
Class T common
stock remains outstanding, the Class T directors and the remaining directors shall be allocated among the
classes so that each class includes a proportionate number of Class T directors and other directors. Upon
expiration of the term of a class of directors, directors for that class would each be elected for a three-year term
at the annual meeting of stockholders in the year in which that term expires. As a result, only one class of
directors would be elected at each annual meeting of our stockholders, with the other classes continuing for the
remainder of their respective three-year terms. Each director’s term would continue until the third annual
meeting of stockholders following their election and until his or her successor has been elected and qualified, or
until his or her earlier death, resignation, or removal. Any increase or decrease in the number of directors
would be distributed among the three classes so that, as nearly as practicable, each class would consist of one-
third of our directors.
Regardless of the class or classes of stock by which a director is elected, there is no limit to the number of terms
a director may serve.
Stockholder Meetings and Actions by Written Consent
Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that will become effective immediately prior to the
completion of this offering will provide that, for so long as our Class F common stock or Class T common stock
remains outstanding, our stockholders may act by written
consent
with respect to certain actions, including any
action to elect or remove directors. Although stockholders will have the ability to take these actions by written
consent, we value the perspectives of all of our stockholders and, in accordance with the listing standards of the
Nasdaq Global Select Market, we expect to hold an annual meeting of stockholders and to solicit the votes of
holders of our Class A common stock in respect of relevant matters to be considered at such meeting, including
the election of our directors who are not Class T directors.

Director Independence and Controlled Company Exemption
Our board of directors has undertaken a review of the independence of each director. Based on information
provided by each director concerning their background, employment, and affiliations, our board of directors
has determined that Mr. Hastings, Mr. Liddell, Dr. Narasimhan and Ms. Razavi do not have a relationship that
would interfere with the exercise of independent judgment in carrying out the responsibilities of a director and
that each of these directors is “independent” as that term is defined under the listing standards of the Nasdaq
Global Select Market. In making these determinations, our board of directors considered the current and prior
relationships that each non-employee director has with our company and all other facts and circumstances our
board of directors deemed relevant in determining their independence, including the beneficial ownership of
our capital stock by each non-employee director, and the transactions involving them described in the section
titled “Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions.”
We are considered a “controlled company” within the meaning of the Nasdaq Global Select Market corporate
governance requirements because the LTBT, as the sole holder of our Class T common stock, generally has the
258
Table of Contents
power to elect a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors. As a result, we may elect not to
comply with certain corporate governance requirements, including:
•
the requirement
that a majority of our board of directors consist of independent directors;
•
the requirement that our board of directors have a nominating and corporate governance committee
that is comprised entirely of independent directors with a written charter addressing the committee’s
purpose and responsibilities; and
•
the requirement that our board of directors have a compensation committee that is comprised entirely
of independent directors with a written charter addressing the committee’s purpose and
responsibilities.
If we elect not to comply with certain requirements, you will not have the same protections afforded to
stockholders of companies that are subject to all of the Nasdaq Global Select Market corporate governance
requirements. Although we qualify as a “controlled company,” we do not expect to rely on this exemption except
with respect to our NGC, which will not consist entirely of independent directors. Our board of directors
currently consists of a majority of independent directors and our audit and compensation committees currently
consist entirely of independent directors. In the event that we cease to be a “controlled company” and our Class
A common stock continues to be listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market, we will be required to comply with
the provision that our NGC be comprised entirely of independent directors within the applicable transition
period.

LTBT’s ability to nominate or remove that director or change the director designated as the Specified Class T

collaboration between the LTBT Trustees and our leadership in identifying and sourcing candidates to serve as

ability to limit the LTBT’s freedom to elect directors of its choosing. However, with respect to the Specified

voting upon a proposal to nominate, remove, or change the Specified Class T Director, the requisite approval of
our Class E common stock will require a majority of votes cast by our Class E common stock and quorum will
require the presence, in person or by proxy, of a majority of the outstanding shares of Class E common stock.

Equity Compensation
Annual Award.
Each non-employee director automatically will be granted, on the date of each annual meeting
of stockholders beginning in 2027, an award of RSUs (the “Annual Award”) with a value of $325,000 (the
“Annual Award Grant Value”), which value will be converted to a number of shares of our Class A common
stock in accordance with then-current standard company practices using the same methodology applied to
employee equity awards pursuant to the company’s equity grant policy, as most recently approved by our board
of directors or a board committee that has been designated appropriate authority (the “Conversion
Methodology”). An Annual Award will vest in four equal quarterly installments on each Quarterly Vesting Date
(as defined below) that occurs following the grant date of the Annual Award provided that, in any event, the
Annual Award will vest in full on the day immediately before the date of our next annual meeting of
stockholders that follows the grant date of the Annual Award, subject to the non-employee director continuing
to be a service provider to us through the applicable vesting date. “Quarterly Vesting Date” means February 20,
May 20, August 20, and November 20 of a given year.
Initial Award and Pro-Rated Annual Award.
Each person who first becomes a non-employee director
following the effective date of the Director Compensation Policy will be automatically granted:
•
An award of RSUs with a value of $400,000, which value will be converted to a number of shares of
our Class A common stock subject to such award using the Conversion Methodology (an “Initial
Award”); and
•
An award of RSUs with a value equal to the Annual Award Grant Value multiplied by the fraction
obtained by dividing (A) the number of full months during the period beginning on the date the
individual first becomes a non-employee director and ending on the one-year anniversary of the date of
our then-most recent annual meeting of stockholders by (B) 12, which will be converted to a number of
shares of our Class A common stock subject to such award using the Conversion Methodology (a “Pro-
Rated Annual Award”).
The grant of each Initial Award and Pro-Rated Annual Award will be made effective on the first trading date on
or after the date on which such individual first becomes a non-employee director (such date, the “Initial Start
Date”). If an individual is a member of our board of directors and also an employee, becoming a non‑employee
director due to termination of employment will not entitle the non-employee director to an Initial Award or a
Pro-Rated Annual Award.
The Initial Award will vest as follows: 12.5% of the RSUs will vest on the six-month anniversary of the Vesting
Commencement Date (as defined below) and the balance of the RSUs will vest in 14 successive equal quarterly
installments on each Quarterly Vesting Date thereafter, subject to the non-employee director remaining a
service provider to us through the applicable vesting date. “Vesting Commencement Date” means the first
Quarterly Vesting Date that occurs on or following the Initial Start Date. The Pro-Rated Annual Award will vest
in equal installments on each Quarterly Vesting Date that occurs between the Initial Start Date and the earlier
of (i) our next annual meeting of stockholders that occurs after the Pro-Rated Annual Award’s grant date or (ii)
the one-year anniversary of our most recent annual meeting of stockholders, provided that, in any event, the
Pro-Rated Annual Award will vest in full on the day immediately before the date of our next annual meeting of
stockholders that occurs after the Pro-Rated Annual Award’s grant date (for purposes of clarity, each such

Table of Contents
Quarterly Vesting Date and the final vest date that occurs on the date immediately before our next annual
meeting of stockholders or one-year anniversary of our most recent annual meeting of stockholders, as
applicable, will be counted as one installment such that, if there are two such Quarterly Vesting Dates, the Pro-
Rated Annual Award shall vest in three equal installments), subject to the non-employee director remaining a

Change in Control
In the event of a “change in control” (as defined in our 2026 Plan), each non-employee director will fully vest in
their outstanding equity awards granted pursuant to the Director Compensation Policy under our 2026 Plan,
including any Initial Award and Pro-Rated Annual Award or Annual Award, provided that the non-employee
director continues to be a non-employee director through such date.

Compensation Discussion and Analysis
The purpose of this Compensation Discussion and Analysis (“CD&A”) section is to discuss our compensation
philosophy, our executive compensation program, and the compensation for our named executive officers
(“NEOs”).
Our NEOs for the year ended December 31, 2025 were:
•
Dario Amodei, our Chief Executive Officer, Co-Founder, and Director;
•
Daniela Amodei, our President, Co-Founder, and Director; and
•
Krishna Rao, our Chief Financial Officer.
This discussion contains forward-looking statements that are based on our current plans, considerations,
expectations, and determinations regarding future compensation programs. See also the section titled “Special
Note Regarding Forward-looking Statements.” Actual compensation programs that we adopt in the future may
differ materially from the currently planned programs summarized in this discussion. For additional
information regarding the compensation programs for, and compensation provided to, our NEOs, see the
section titled “—Post-Fiscal Year End Compensation Changes and Equity Awards.”
Executive Summary
At Anthropic, we strive to build a team that is aligned with our mission and values. Executive compensation
reflects our overall compensation philosophy, which prioritizes competitive pay that targets the 90th percentile
of the AI development market, consistent pay for the same role, level, and location, and simplicity of plan
design. In 2025, we offered a competitive mix of base salary, long-term equity incentive awards (including stock
options and RSUs), and other benefits to attract and retain top talent in a competitive market environment.
Compensation Philosophy and Objectives
Our executive compensation philosophy is to provide our executive officers with consistent cash and equity
compensation for the same role, level, and location. When determining executive compensation, we review each
executive’s current compensation against role- and level-specific market data. We do this bi-annually as part of
our performance and compensation cycle where we review proposed market-based and promotion-based cash
and equity increases for executives. We plan to continue to regularly review, and potentially adjust, our
executive compensation programs to ensure they are consistent with our compensation philosophy as a public
company.
In determining compensation for our senior leaders, we distinguish between our seven co-founders (among
whom only Dr. Amodei and Ms. Amodei are executive officers) and our other senior leaders who are not co-
founders (among whom only Mr. Rao is an executive officer). Each co-founder is paid equal compensation. As a
non-co-founder senior leader, Mr. Rao received base salary and equity compensation based on market data for
his role and level.
Our executive compensation program is structured to achieve the objectives described below. We regularly
review our executive compensation program to assess whether it meets these objectives and adapts to evolving
economic conditions.
•
Competitive Pay to Attract and Retain Top Talent.
We provide our executives with competitive cash
and equity pay for each role, location, and level to attract mission-aligned, top executive talent.
•
Internal Parity.
We take internal parity into account when determining executive compensation. As
co-founders, Dr. Amodei and Ms. Amodei are awarded equal compensation, including any annual cash
or equity increases. As a non-co-founder senior leader, Mr. Rao is compensated based on the market
265
Table of Contents
data from our peer group for his role, level, and location. We review market data twice a year and make
adjustments to our compensation benchmarks as needed.
•
Aligning Executive Interests with Our Stockholders.
We provide incentives that seek to align our
executives’ interests with those of our stockholders through long-term equity awards, which vest over
time.

Executive Compensation Process
Role of the Board of Directors and Compensation Committee
Our executive compensation program has historically been overseen by the non-employee members of our
board of directors, which, as a group, has made decisions regarding the compensation for our NEOs after
considering recommendations from management, as further discussed below.
Following the completion of this offering, the compensation committee of our board of directors will oversee
our executive compensation program and provide recommendations to our board of directors on compensation
decisions for our executive officers. The compensation committee will work closely with its independent
compensation consultant (engaged in connection with this offering, as described below) and meet regularly to
make decisions on our executive compensation program. We expect that our compensation committee will
review a variety of market data and information, including survey data, and consider the recommendations of
its independent compensation consultant when making compensation decisions. Following the completion of
this offering, the compensation committee’s responsibilities will include, among other things, reviewing and
approving (or making recommendations to our board of directors, as applicable): overall compensation
strategy; amounts and form of executive compensation; goals and objectives to be considered in determining
the compensation of our Chief Executive Officer and other executive officers; annual and long-term incentive
plans and benefit plans; board of directors compensation; whether such compensation policies and practices
create risks that are reasonably likely to have a material adverse effect on the company; annual say-on-pay vote
results; annual proxy and CD&A disclosure; and compensation peer group.
Role of Management
Our Chief Executive Officer and our other executive officers do not set their own compensation, nor are they
present when our board of directors sets their individual compensation. Our President reviews and advises on
compensation for the seven co-founders but does not make specific recommendations on or participate in
decisions related to her compensation or our Chief Executive Officer’s compensation. Our President also
provides her evaluation and makes recommendations with respect to base salary and equity awards for each
266
Table of Contents
other executive officer, which are considered by our board of directors as it ultimately makes its determinations.
Our people team provides further analysis and feedback as requested by our board of directors with regard to
the compensation of our executives.
Role of Independent Compensation Consultant
In connection with this offering, we have engaged Semler Brossy Consulting Group LLC as an independent
compensation consultant to formalize our post-offering compensation programs and implement compensation
arrangements that reflect our compensation philosophy described above.

Base Salary
Our board of directors generally reviews the base salaries of our NEOs twice a year. The factors used to
determine base salary for our executives include market data for the role, level, and location, as well as internal
parity (which, for our co-founder NEOs, includes considerations related to parity with our technical leadership).
From January 1, 2025 to June 15, 2025, the annual base salary for each of Dr. Amodei and Ms. Amodei was
$600,000. Effective June 16, 2025, the annual base salary for each of Dr. Amodei and Ms. Amodei was
increased to $700,000. The increase in the executives’ cash compensation was intended to ensure competitive
and equitable compensation for our leaders. In particular, the salary increases recognized their ongoing
leadership roles, while considering relative parity across executives, including our technical leadership.
From January 1, 2025 to December 15, 2025, the annual base salary for Mr. Rao was $700,000, which was
increased to $850,000 effective December 16, 2025. The salary increase was based on market data for Mr.
Rao’s role and level, as well as internal parity for non-co-founder senior leaders who are not executive officers.
Long-Term Equity Incentive Program
Each year, our NEOs are eligible to receive equity awards under our 2021 Plan. By structuring the majority of
our NEOs’ target total direct compensation payable in the form of equity that vests over a number of years, we
create incentives for our NEOs to remain employed with Anthropic and pursue actions that will benefit our
company and stockholders over the long term.

Perquisites and Other Executive
Benefits
We generally provide the same benefits to all of our employees, including our NEOs, and generally do not
maintain benefit plans that cover only executive officers or provide perquisites or personal benefits to our
NEOs. However, we do provide certain travel and security benefits to some of our NEOs. These benefits are
described in more detail below. Our board of directors believes these benefits are reasonable and necessary, and
for the benefit of our company. These benefits are intended to promote the productivity of our executives, in
addition to ensuring their personal health, safety, and security. The aggregate incremental cost of providing
these benefits to our NEOs is disclosed in the “All Other Compensation” column of the Summary Compensation
Table.
Travel
We maintain a Travel and Expense Policy (the “Travel Policy”), which outlines guidelines and allowances for
executive travel and expenses, recognizing the needs and responsibilities of our senior leadership team. The
Travel Policy governs all business-related travel and expenses for our executives, except to the extent benefits
are provided through a security program authorized and/or approved by our board of directors. Dr. Amodei
and Ms. Amodei are entitled to certain enhanced travel benefits recommended by the
security studies on which
their security program is based
(discussed in the section below titled “Security Services”). The Travel Policy is
reviewed annually by our management team to ensure it remains appropriate and aligned with company
objectives and industry standards. To the extent required by the relevant tax laws, the value of any personal use,
including any personal elements of business trips, will be treated as taxable compensation to the executive, and
268
Table of Contents
we do not cover, reimburse, or otherwise “gross-up” any income tax due from any applicable executive on such
compensation.
Except as noted in the subsection below titled “Security Services,” none of our NEOs were provided with private
aviation services for personal travel in 2025.
Security Services
The protection of our senior leadership is a critical priority for our company and our stockholders. In
connection with our security program and our evaluation of security threats, we offer security services to certain
of our NEOs and may provide security services to other NEOs in the future. Such security services may include:
(i) individual protection services (including the protection of family members) and home security systems and
monitoring, (ii) private aviation, and (iii) private car and driver services. These safeguards are implemented due
to the variety of business-related security concerns faced by our senior leaders, and they are comparable to
those provided to senior leaders of comparable high-profile companies in the technology industry.
In 2025, a leading security consulting firm conducted independent, third-party security studies regarding the
personal and security risks of our Chief Executive Officer and our President. Based on these security studies,
increased media attention for Anthropic, and the identification of bona fide business-related, heightened
security concerns arising as a result of the respective positions of Dr. Amodei and Ms. Amodei within the
company, our board of directors determined that enhanced personal security services were necessary to
increase the safety and protection of Dr. Amodei and Ms. Amodei, and to avoid an impact to our business
continuity if a security incident occurred. Our board of directors regularly assesses security concerns and
reviews the security services provided to Dr. Amodei and Ms. Amodei and the cost of such services in light of
such concerns, and other benefits to our company. The security measures for Dr. Amodei and Ms. Amodei in
2025 included (i) individual protection services (including during personal travel), which included the
protection of family members, as well as enhanced home security systems and surveillance, (ii) private car and
driver services for ground transportation, and (iii) in the case of Dr. Amodei, the use of private aircraft for both
business and personal travel.
Given the importance of the roles of Dr. Amodei and Ms. Amodei at Anthropic, our board of directors required
the security measures described above for the benefit of our company, and we view the costs of these services as
necessary and appropriate. In the “All Other Compensation” column of the Summary Compensation Table, we
have disclosed the aggregate incremental cost of the security benefits that may be deemed to be perquisites
under current relevant disclosure rules. We did not pay expenses for personal security for any other NEOs in
2025, except in connection with business-related travel.

Other Compensation Governance Practices
Compensation Recovery Policy
We have adopted an executive compensation recoupment policy intended to comply with the requirements of
Rule 10D-1 under the Exchange Act and the rules of the stock exchange on which our securities are listed
(“Clawback Policy”) that will be effective upon the effectiveness of the registration statement of which this
prospectus forms a part. The Clawback Policy will generally require us to recover erroneously awarded
incentive-based compensation that was received by covered executive officers in the event we are required to
prepare an accounting restatement due to any material noncompliance with any financial reporting
requirement under the securities laws (including any required accounting restatement to correct an error in
previously issued financial statements that is material to the previously issued financial statements), or that
would result in a material misstatement if the error were corrected in the current period or left uncorrected in
the current period. The Clawback Policy generally covers incentive-based compensation received on or after the
effective date of the Clawback Policy and during the three-year period prior to the date we are required to
prepare the financial restatement. The amount required to be recovered is the excess of the amount of
incentive-based compensation received over the amount that otherwise would have been received based on the
restated financial measure.
Hedging, Pledging, and Insider Trading
We are dedicated to fostering high standards of ethical business conduct and adherence to applicable laws,
rules, and regulations. Accordingly, we maintain our Insider Trading Policy, which we believe is appropriately
270
Table of Contents
designed to foster compliance with insider trading laws, rules, and regulations, and the listing standards of the
Nasdaq Global Select Market that will be applicable to us. Our Insider Trading Policy applies to all of our
officers, directors, and employees, as well as designated consultants, and specifically prohibits ownership of
financial instruments or participation in investment strategies that hedge the economic risk of owning our
equity securities, such as prepaid variable forwards, equity swaps, and collars. Directors, officers, and other
employees are prohibited from maintaining company securities in a margin account or otherwise pledging
company securities as collateral for a loan, provided that certain limited exceptions may be permitted. In
addition, we prohibit our executive officers, directors, and employees from purchasing or selling our securities
while in possession of material, non-public information or otherwise utilizing such information for their
personal benefit. We maintain a quarterly blackout window where applicable individuals may not trade.
Policies and Practices Related to the Grant of Certain Equity Awards Close in Time to the
Release of Material Nonpublic Information
We periodically grant stock options to our NEOs, employees, and other service providers. We have historically
granted options on or shortly after a newly hired employee’s start date. We have historically granted refresh,
promotion, or market adjustment options when and as determined by our board of directors. We have no
specific policy or practice regarding the timing of options or other equity grants in relation to the public
disclosure of material nonpublic information by the company.
Tax and Accounting Considerations
Tax Considerations
Section 162(m) of the Code imposes a $1 million limit on the amount of compensation that we may deduct as a
business expense in any year with regard to certain of our most highly paid executive officers. While our board
of directors considers the deductibility of compensation as one factor in determining executive compensation,
our board of directors retains the discretion to award compensation that is not deductible as it believes that it is
in our best interests to maintain flexibility in our approach to executive compensation in order to design a
program that we deem to be the most effective in attracting, motivating, and retaining key executives and
aligning pay with performance.
Accounting Considerations
Our board of directors takes accounting considerations into account in designing compensation plans and
arrangements for our NEOs and other employees. We follow the Financial Accounting Standards Board’s
Accounting Standards Codification Topic 718 (“FASB ASC Topic 718”) for our stock-based compensation
awards. FASB ASC Topic 718 requires us to measure the compensation expense for all share-based payment
awards based on the grant date “fair value” of these awards.

Perquisites and Other Executive Benefits
HSR Filing Fees
In October 2026, we paid directly to the FTC, on behalf of Dr. Amodei and Ms. Amodei, the filing fees that they
were required to pay in connection with the filing of a notice under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust
Improvements Act of 1976, as amended, each in the amount of $2.5 million (the “HSR Filing Fees”). The HSR
Filing Fees were required in connection with the NEO’s acquisition and holding of our securities. Our board of
directors determined that paying the HSR Filing Fees served the best interest of us and our stockholders by
ensuring compliance with antitrust regulations and promoting each NEO’s retention and long-term stockholder
value alignment by providing incentives for each NEO to participate in our long-term equity incentive program
and work to increase the value of our securities.
Security Services
In 2026, we began offering certain security services to Mr. Rao and engaged a leading security consulting firm
to conduct an independent, third-party security study regarding the personal and security risks of Mr. Rao.
Given the importance of the role of Mr. Rao at Anthropic, we view the cost of these services as necessary and
appropriate.

Employment, Severance, and Change of Control Arrangements with Our
NEOs
We entered into an offer letter with Mr. Rao dated March 2, 2024, which provided for “at-will” employment and
included his initial base salary, a new hire stock option grant, and severance and change of control benefits. The
Rao Offer Letter was in effect during 2025 and was terminated in October 2026.
Specifically, the Rao Offer Letter provided that if, at any time, his employment was terminated by the company
without “cause” or he resigned for “good reason” (as such terms are defined in the Rao Offer Letter), then,
subject to his execution of a release of claims in favor of the company, his compliance with his confidential
information and invention assignment agreement and all material company policies, and his return of company
property, he would be eligible to receive the following severance payments and benefits: (i) an amount equal to
six months of his then-current base salary, (ii) payment of monthly premiums for coverage under COBRA for
up to six months, and (iii) accelerated vesting as to 1/8
th
of the Rao Options.
The Rao Offer Letter further provided that if, within 30 days prior to, upon or at any time following a “change of
control” (as defined in
our
2021 Plan), his employment was terminated by the company without cause or he
resigns for good reason, then, subject to his execution of a release of claims in favor of the company and his
return of company property, 100% of any then-unvested shares subject to his then-outstanding equity awards,
including the Rao Options, would accelerate and vest. If, in the change of control, his then-outstanding equity
awards would otherwise have been terminated for no consideration at the closing of the change of control event,
then those awards would instead become fully vested as of immediately prior to such closing.
Upon the
termination of the Rao Offer Letter in October 2026, we entered into a letter agreement with Mr. Rao
continuing the change of control vesting acceleration benefit described herein on the same terms, without
alteration.

Equity Plans
2026 Equity Incentive Plan
General.
Our 2026 Plan was adopted by our board of directors on September 1, 2026, and approved by our
stockholders
on
October 22
, 2026
. Our 2026 Plan will become effective as of the day immediately prior to the
day the registration statement of which this prospectus forms a part is effective.
Share Reserve.
The maximum aggregate number of shares that may be issued under our 2026 Plan is: (i)
shares of our Class A common stock; plus (ii) the number of shares of our Class A common stock equal to the
total shares of Voting Common Stock available for issuance pursuant to our 2021 Plan immediately prior to the
termination of our 2021 Plan on the effective date of our 2026 Plan; plus (iii) the number of shares of our Class
A common stock equal to the total shares of Voting Common Stock subject to awards previously granted under
our 2021 Plan that, after the effective date of our 2026 Plan, would have returned to our 2021 Plan and become
available for issuance pursuant to future awards under our 2021 Plan had our 2021 Plan not terminated on the
effective date of our 2026 Plan (provided that the maximum number of shares pursuant to (ii) plus (iii) is
shares).
In addition, the number of shares that may be issued under our 2026 Plan will be increased on the first day of
each fiscal year beginning with our 2027 fiscal year and ending on (and including) the first day of our 2036
fiscal year, in an amount equal to the lesser of: (i) 5% of the total number of shares of our common stock
(including only all classes of common stock issued by the company that carry economic rights) outstanding on
the last day of the calendar month prior to the date of such automatic increase (calculated on an as-converted
basis); and (ii) such number of shares determined by our board of directors.
To the extent an award should expire or be forfeited or become unexercisable for any reason without having
been exercised in full, or is surrendered pursuant to an exchange program, the unissued shares that were
subject thereto shall continue to be available under our 2026 Plan for issuance pursuant to future awards. In
276
Table of Contents
addition, any shares which are retained by us to satisfy exercise or purchase price or any withholding taxes shall
be treated as not issued and shall continue to be available under our 2026 Plan for issuance pursuant to future
awards. Shares issued under our 2026 Plan and later forfeited to us due to the failure to vest or repurchased by
us at a price no greater than the original purchase price paid to us for the shares shall again be available for
future grant under our 2026 Plan. To the extent an award under our 2026 Plan is paid out in cash rather than
shares, such cash payment will not reduce the number of shares available for issuance under our 2026 Plan.
Plan Administration.
Our board of directors has delegated its authority to administer our 2026 Plan to our
compensation committee. Subject to the provisions of our 2026 Plan, the administrator has the power to
determine the terms of awards, including the recipients, the exercise price, if any, the number of shares subject
to each award, the fair market value of a share of our Class A common stock, the vesting schedule applicable to
the awards, together with any vesting acceleration, the form of consideration, if any, payable upon exercise of
the award and the terms of the award agreement for use under our 2026 Plan. The administrator also has the
authority, subject to the terms of our 2026 Plan, to amend existing awards, to prescribe rules and to construe
and interpret our 2026 Plan and awards granted thereunder and to institute an exchange program by which
outstanding awards are amended to provide for a lower exercise price or surrendered or cancelled in exchange
for awards with a lower exercise price, a different type of award under our 2026 Plan or a different equity
incentive plan, cash, or a combination thereof.
Eligibility.
Employees, members of our board of directors who are not employees, and consultants (including,
without limitation, employees of a staffing agency, professional employer organization, employer of record, and
similar workers) are eligible to participate in our 2026 Plan.
Types of Awards.
Our 2026 Plan provides for the grant of stock options, stock appreciation rights, restricted
stock, restricted stock units, and stock bonus awards to our employees, directors, and consultants and the
employees and consultants of our subsidiaries.
Stock Options.
The administrator may grant incentive stock options (within the meaning of Section 422 of the
Code) and/or nonstatutory stock options under our 2026 Plan, provided that incentive stock options may only
be granted to our employees and the employees of our subsidiaries. The exercise price applicable to such
options must generally be equal to at least the fair market value of our Class A common stock on the date of
grant. The term of an incentive stock option may not exceed 10 years; provided, however, that an incentive
stock option held by a participant who owns more than 10% of the total combined voting power of all classes of
our stock, or of certain of our subsidiary corporations, may not have a term in excess of five years and must
have an exercise price equal to at least 110% of the fair market value of our Class A common stock on the grant
date.
The administrator will determine the methods of payment of the exercise price applicable to an option, which
may include cash, shares, or other property acceptable to the administrator. Subject to the provisions of our
2026 Plan, the administrator determines the remaining terms of the options. Such terms may include, among
other things, vesting upon the achievement of specific performance goals determined by the administrator and/
or continued service. After the termination of service, the participant may exercise their option, to the extent
vested, for the period of time stated in their option agreement. Except in the event of a termination for cause,
options generally remain outstanding to the extent exercisable for the full term of the options. In no event may
an option be exercised later than the expiration of its term. The specific terms will be set forth in an award
agreement.
Stock Appreciation Rights.
Stock appreciation rights may be granted under our 2026 Plan. Stock appreciation
rights allow the recipient to receive the appreciation in the fair market value of our Class A common stock
between the date of grant and the exercise date. Subject to the provisions of our 2026 Plan, the administrator
determines the terms of stock appreciation rights, including when such rights vest and become exercisable and
whether to settle such awards in cash or with shares of our Class A common stock, or a combination thereof,
except that the per share exercise price for the shares to be issued pursuant to the exercise of a stock
appreciation right will be no less than 100% of the fair market value per share on the date of grant. The specific
terms will be set forth in an award agreement.
Restricted Stock.
Restricted stock may be granted under our 2026 Plan. RSAs are grants of shares of our Class
A common stock that are subject to various restrictions, including restrictions on transferability and forfeiture
277
Table of Contents
provisions. Shares of restricted stock will vest and the restrictions on such shares will lapse, in accordance with
terms and conditions established by the administrator. Such terms may include, among other things, vesting
upon the achievement of specific performance goals determined by the administrator and/or continued service.
The administrator, in its sole discretion, may accelerate the time at which any restrictions will lapse or be
removed. Recipients of RSAs generally will have voting and dividend rights with respect to such shares upon
grant without regard to vesting, unless the administrator provides otherwise. Shares of restricted stock that do
not vest for any reason will be subject to our right of repurchase or forfeited by the recipient. The specific terms
will be set forth in an award agreement.
Restricted Stock Units.
RSUs may be granted under our 2026 Plan and may include the right to dividend
equivalents, as determined in the discretion of the administrator. Each RSU granted is a bookkeeping entry
representing an amount equal to the fair market value of one share of our Class A common stock. The
administrator determines the terms and conditions of RSUs, including the vesting criteria, which may include
achievement of specified performance criteria and/or continued service. The administrator, in its sole
discretion, may accelerate the time at which any restrictions will lapse or be removed. The administrator
determines, in its sole discretion, the timing of payment and whether an award will be settled in stock, cash, or
a combination thereof. The specific terms will be set forth in an award agreement.
Stock Bonus
Awards. Stock bonus awards may be granted under our 2026 Plan. The administrator may grant
stock bonus awards in such amounts, and subject to such terms, as the administrator, in its sole discretion, will
determine. A stock bonus award is an award of shares of our Class A common stock without a purchase price.
All stock bonus awards may be made, but are not required to be made, pursuant to an award agreement.
Payment of a stock bonus award may be made in the form of cash, shares, or a combination thereof, based on
the fair market value of the shares subject to the stock bonus award on the date of payment, as determined in
the sole discretion of the administrator.
Outside Director Limitations.
Stock awards granted during a single fiscal year under our 2026 Plan or
otherwise, taken together with any cash fees paid during such fiscal year for services on our board of directors,
shall not exceed $1,000,000 in total value for any non-employee director, except with respect to the first year of
service in which case any stock awards granted and cash fees paid will not exceed $2,000,000 in total value
(calculating the value of any such stock awards, in each case, based on the grant date fair value of such stock
awards for financial reporting purposes). Such applicable limit includes the value of any stock awards that are
granted in lieu of all or a portion of any annual committee cash retainers or other similar cash-based payments.
Stock awards granted to an individual while they were serving in the capacity as an employee or while they were
an independent contractor but not a non-employee director will not count for purposes of the limitations
described above.
Non-Transferability of Awards.
Unless the administrator provides otherwise, our 2026 Plan generally does not
allow for the transfer of awards other than by will or the laws of descent and distribution and only the recipient
of an option or stock appreciation right may exercise such an award during their lifetime.
Certain Adjustments.
In the event of a stock split, reverse stock split, stock dividend, combination,
consolidation, recapitalization (including a recapitalization through a large nonrecurring cash dividend or
distribution of property, including shares of a subsidiary) or reclassification of the shares, subdivision of the
shares, a rights offering, a reorganization, merger, spin-off, split-up, repurchase, or exchange of common stock
or other securities of the company or other significant corporate transaction, or other change affecting the
common stock occurs, the administrator, in order to prevent dilution, diminution, or enlargement of the
benefits or potential benefits intended to be made available under our 2026 Plan, will, in such manner as it may
deem equitable, adjust the number, kind, and class of securities that may be delivered under our 2026 Plan
and/or the number, class, kind, and price of securities covered by each outstanding award, and the terms and
conditions of any outstanding award (including, without limitation, any applicable performance targets or
criteria with respect thereto).
Dissolution or Liquidation.
In the event of a proposed winding up, dissolution, or liquidation of the company,
the administrator will notify participants as soon as practicable prior to the effective date of such proposed
transaction and all awards will terminate immediately prior to the consummation of such proposed transaction,
to the extent not previously exercised or settled.

Table of Contents
Corporate Transaction.
Our 2026 Plan provides that, in the event of certain significant corporate transactions,
including: (1) a transfer of all or substantially all of our assets; (2) a merger, consolidation or other capital
reorganization or business combination transaction of the company with or into another corporation, entity or
person; or (3) the consummation of a transaction, or series of related transactions, in which any person
becomes the beneficial owner, directly or indirectly, of more than 50% of the company’s then outstanding
capital stock, each outstanding award will be treated as the administrator determines. Such determination,
without the consent of any participant, may provide that such awards will be (i) continued if we are the
surviving corporation; (ii) assumed by the surviving corporation or its parent; (iii) substituted by the surviving
corporation or its parent for a new award; (iv) cancelled in exchange for a payment equal to the excess of the
fair market value of our shares subject to such award over the exercise price or purchase price paid for such
shares; (v) subject to full or partial acceleration of vesting, settlement, payment, and/or expiration as of
immediately prior to the corporate transaction; (vi) subject to full or partial lapse of forfeiture, repurchase or
reacquisition rights with respect to shares previously acquired pursuant to any awards as of immediately prior
to the corporate transaction; (vii) in the case of outstanding options and/or stock appreciation rights, allowed to
be exercised prior to the occurrence of the corporate transaction and terminated (for no consideration) upon
the consummation of such corporate transaction if not exercised prior thereto; or (viii) cancelled in exchange
for no consideration.
Change in Control.
The administrator may provide, in an individual award agreement or in any other written
agreement between a participant and us, that the stock award will be subject to additional acceleration of
vesting, settlement, payment, and/or expiration in the event of a change in control.
Under our 2026 Plan, a “change in control” is generally (1) a merger, consolidation, or any other corporate
reorganization in which the shares of capital stock of the company immediately before the transaction cease to
represent immediately after such transaction at least a majority of the voting power of the continuing or
surviving entity in substantially the same proportions immediately after such transaction as in effect before
such transaction; (2) with certain limited exceptions, the consummation of the sale, transfer or other
disposition of all or substantially all of our assets; (3) a change in the effective control of the company which
occurs on the date that a majority of our board members are replaced during any 12-month period by directors
whose appointment or election is not endorsed by a majority of the members of our board of directors prior to
the date of the appointment or election; or (4) the consummation of any transaction as a result of which any
person or company becomes the beneficial owner, directly or indirectly, of at least 50% of the total voting power
represented by our then outstanding voting securities. No transaction shall constitute a change in control (i) as
the result of the initial effectiveness of the company’s amended and restated certificate of incorporation that
will become effective immediately prior to the effectiveness of the registration statement of which this
prospectus forms a part, (ii) pursuant to Section (3) above until after the time at which both the Class F Sunset
Time and the Class T Sunset Time have occurred, as such terms are defined in the company’s amended and
restated certificate of incorporation that will become effective immediately prior to the effectiveness of the
registration statement of which this prospectus forms a part, (iii) if its primary purpose is to change the
jurisdiction of the company’s incorporation or to create a holding company owned in substantially the same
proportions by the persons who held company securities immediately before such transactions, or (iv) if
required for compliance with Section 409A of the Code, a transaction will not be a change in control unless it is
also a “change in the ownership or effective control of” the company or “a change in the ownership of a
substantial portion of the assets of” the company as determined under applicable Treasury regulations.
Compensation Recovery Policy.
Awards granted under our 2026 Plan will be subject to reduction, cancellation,
forfeiture, and/or recoupment in accordance with any compensation recovery policy as may be in effect as of
the date of grant of such award, or as such policy is amended or another policy is adopted to comply with
applicable laws. In addition, the administrator may impose such other compensation recovery or recoupment
provisions in any award agreement as it determines necessary or appropriate.
Amendment or Termination.
Our administrator has the authority to amend, alter, suspend, or terminate our
2026 Plan, provided such action does not materially impair the existing rights of any participant unless
otherwise provided in our 2026 Plan or mutually agreed otherwise. Our 2026 Plan will continue in effect until
terminated by the administrator, but no options that qualify as incentive stock options may be granted after 10
years from the earlier of the board or stockholder approval of our 2026 Plan. We will obtain stockholder
approval of any amendment to our 2026 Plan as required by applicable law or listing requirements.

General.

effective as of May 28, 2026. Our 2021 Plan will be terminated effective as of the day immediately prior to the
day the registration statement of which this prospectus forms a part becomes effective, and no new awards will
be granted under our 2021 Plan following this offering, but previously granted awards will continue to be
subject to the terms and conditions of our 2021 Plan and the award agreements evidencing such awards.
Share Reserve.
We have reserved for issuance pursuant to our 2021 Plan an aggregate of
3,864,826,090
shares
of our Class A common stock. In general, if an award granted under our 2021 Plan (i) expires or is terminated,
cancelled, or otherwise forfeited by a participant, (ii) a share subject to an award is withheld in satisfaction of
the exercise price and/or tax withholding due in connection with such award, or (iii) a share previously issued
pursuant to an award is forfeited or repurchased at the original purchase price paid for the share, then the
number of unissued shares subject to any such award, and any such withheld, forfeited, or repurchased shares,
will again become available for awards under our 2021 Plan. Following the effectiveness of our 2026 Plan, such
shares will again become available for awards under our 2026 Plan.
Plan Administration.
Our board of directors has administered our 2021 Plan before this offering. Our board of
directors has delegated its authority to administer our 2021 Plan to our compensation committee following this
offering.
Types of Awards.
Our 2021 Plan provides for incentive and non-statutory stock options to purchase shares of
our Class A common stock, RSAs, and RSUs. As of the date of this prospectus, we have issued stock options,
restricted stock, and RSUs pursuant to our 2021 Plan.
Non-transferability of Awards.
Unless the administrator provides otherwise, our 2021 Plan generally does not
allow for the transfer of awards other than by will or the laws of descent and distribution and only the recipient
of an option right may exercise such an award during their lifetime.
Certain Adjustments.
In the event of certain corporate events or changes in our capitalization, to prevent
diminution or enlargement of the benefits or potential benefits available under our 2021 Plan, the
administrator will make adjustments to one or more of the number, kind, and class of securities that may be
delivered under our 2021 Plan and/or the number, kind, class, and price of securities covered by each
outstanding award.
Corporate Transaction.
Our 2021 Plan provides that in the event of (i) a transfer of all or substantially all of our
assets, (ii) a merger, consolidation, or other capital reorganization or business combination transaction of us
with or into another corporation, entity, or person, or (iii) the consummation of a transaction, or series of
related transactions, in which any “person” becomes the “beneficial owner,” directly or indirectly, of more than
50% of our then outstanding capital stock (each, a “Corporate Transaction”), the administrator may, in its sole
and absolute discretion and without the need for the consent of any participant, take one or more of the
following actions contingent upon the occurrence of that Corporate Transaction with respect to outstanding
awards granted under our 2021 Plan which provide for: (A) the continuation of such awards by us (if we are the
surviving corporation); (B) the assumption of such awards by the surviving corporation or its parent; (C) the
substitution by the surviving corporation or its parent of new options or equity awards for such awards; (D) the
cancellation of such awards in exchange for a payment to the participants equal to the excess of (1) the fair
market value of the shares or units subject to such awards as of the closing date of such Corporate Transaction
over (2) the exercise price or purchase price paid or to be paid for the shares or units representing shares
subject to the awards, as applicable; or (E) the cancellation of any outstanding awards or an outstanding right
to purchase restricted stock, in either case, for no consideration.
Amendment or Termination.
Our board of directors may amend or terminate our 2021 Plan at any time. If our
board of directors amends our 2021 Plan, we will ask our stockholders to approve the amendment if such
approval is necessary or desirable to comply with applicable law. No further awards will be made under our
2021 Plan after this offering.

2026 Employee Stock Purchase Plan
General.
Our ESPP was adopted by our board of directors on September 1, 2026, and approved by our
stockholders on October 22
,
2026. Our ESPP will become effective as of the day immediately prior to the day
the registration statement of which this prospectus forms a part is effective.
Our ESPP includes two components: a 423 component and a non‑423 component. We intend the 423
component to qualify as an “employee stock purchase plan” within the meaning of Section 423 of the Code. The
non-423 component authorizes grants of purchase rights that do not comply with Section 423 of the Code.
Share Reserve.
The maximum aggregate number of shares that may be issued under our ESPP is
shares
of our Class A common stock.
In addition, the number of shares that may be issued under our ESPP will be increased on the first day of each
fiscal year beginning with our 2027 fiscal year and ending on (and including) the first day of our 2036 fiscal
year, in an amount equal to the lesser of: (i) 1% of the total number of shares of our common stock (including
only all classes of common stock issued by the company that carry economic rights) outstanding on the last day
of the calendar month prior to the date of such automatic increase (calculated on an as-converted basis); and
(ii) such number of shares determined by our board of directors.
Plan Administration.
Our ESPP is administered by our board of directors or a committee designated by our
board of directors. Our board of directors has delegated its authority to administer our ESPP to our
compensation committee.
Eligibility.
Generally, all regular employees, including executive officers, employed by us or by any of our
designated affiliates and specified service providers (including non-U.S. service providers) of the company or
our designated affiliates may participate in our ESPP.
Employees may have to satisfy one or more of the following service requirements before participating in the 423
components of our ESPP, as determined by the administrator, including: (1) continuous service with us or one
of our affiliates for at least two years (or such lesser period of time as may be determined by our board of
directors), (2) being customarily employed for more than 20 hours per week (or such lesser period of time as
may be determined by our board of directors), (3) being customarily employed for more than five months per
calendar year (or such lesser period of time as may be determined by our board of directors), (4) is not a highly
compensated employee within the meaning of Section 423(b)(4)(D) of the Code, or (5) such other criteria as our
board of directors may determine to be consistent with Section 423 of the Code. No employee may purchase
shares under the 423 component of our ESPP at a rate in excess of $25,000 worth of our Class A common stock
based on the fair market value per share of our Class A common stock at the beginning of an offering for each
year such a purchase right is outstanding. Finally, no employee will be eligible for the grant of any purchase
rights under the 423 component of our ESPP if immediately after such rights are granted, such employee has
voting power over 5% or more of our outstanding capital stock measured by vote or value under Section 424(d)
of the Code.
Offerings.
Our ESPP is implemented through offerings pursuant to which participants are granted rights to
purchase shares of our Class A common stock on specified dates during such offerings. Under our ESPP, we
may specify offerings with durations of not more than 27 months and may specify shorter purchase periods
within each offering. Each offering will have one or more purchase dates on which shares of our Class A
common stock will be purchased by participants in the offering. An offering under our ESPP may be terminated
under certain circumstances. The administrator will have the discretion to structure an offering so that if the
fair market value of a share of our Class A common stock on the first trading day of a new purchase period
within that offering is less than or equal to the fair market value of a share of our Class A common stock on the
offering date for that offering, then that offering will terminate immediately as of that first trading day, and the
participants in such terminated offering will be automatically enrolled in a new offering beginning on the first
trading day of such new offering.
Payroll Deductions.
Participants who are employees may generally make contributions through payroll
deductions (unless otherwise required by law or provided for in an offering). In the case of an offering under the
423 component, such percentage or maximum dollar amount of contributions may not exceed 15% of their
281
Table of Contents
earnings for the applicable offering. Contributions pursuant to the non-423 component will generally be made
on an after-tax basis in a manner determined by the administrator.
Shares of our Class A common stock will be purchased for the accounts of participants in our ESPP at a price
per share that is not less than the lesser of (1) 85% of the fair market value of a share of our Class A common
stock on the first date of an offering, or (2) 85% of the fair market value of a share of our Class A common stock
on the date of purchase.
Certain Adjustments.
In the event of any change that is made in, or other events that occur with respect to, our
Class A common stock subject to our ESPP or subject to any purchase right without the receipt of consideration
by the company through merger, consolidation, reorganization, recapitalization, reincorporation, stock
dividend, dividend in property other than cash, large nonrecurring cash dividend, stock split, liquidating
dividend, combination of shares, exchange of shares, change in corporate structure, or other similar equity
restructuring transaction, our board of directors will make appropriate and proportionate adjustments to: (1)
the class(es) and maximum number of shares reserved under our ESPP, (2) the class(es) and maximum number
of shares by which the share reserve may increase automatically each year, (3) the class(es) and number of
shares subject to, and purchase price applicable to, all outstanding offerings and purchase rights, and (4) the
class(es) and number of shares that are subject to purchase limits under ongoing offerings.
Dissolution or Liquidation.
In the event of a dissolution or liquidation of the company, any offering then in
progress will be shortened by setting a new purchase date prior to the consummation of such proposed
dissolution or liquidation. The board of directors will notify each participant that the purchase date has been
changed and that the participant’s purchase right will be exercised automatically on the new purchase date
unless prior to such date the participant has withdrawn from the offering.
Corporate Transactions.
Our ESPP provides that in the event of certain significant corporate transactions,
including: (1) a transfer of all or substantially all of our assets; (2) a merger, consolidation, or other capital,
reorganization or business combination transaction of the company with or into another corporation, entity, or
person; or (3) the consummation of a transaction, or series of related transactions, in which any person
becomes the beneficial owner, directly or indirectly, of more than 50% of our then outstanding capital stock, a
successor corporation may assume, continue, or substitute each outstanding purchase right. If the successor
corporation does not assume, continue, or substitute the purchase right, the participants’ accumulated
contributions will be used to purchase shares prior to the corporate transaction and the purchase rights will
terminate immediately after such purchase. The administrator will notify each participant that the purchase
date has been changed and that the participant’s purchase right will be exercised automatically on the new
purchase date unless prior to such date the participant has withdrawn from the offering.
Spin-Off.
In the event of a spin-off or similar transaction, our board of directors may take actions deemed
necessary or appropriate in connection with any ongoing offering, subject to compliance with applicable laws.
In the absence of any such action, if an entity ceases to qualify as a related company under our ESPP, any
participant in an ongoing offering employed by, or providing services to, such entity will be treated in the same
manner as if the participant had terminated employment or service.
Amendment or Termination.
Our board of directors has the authority to amend, suspend, or terminate our
ESPP at any time, except that, subject to certain exceptions described in our ESPP, no such action may
materially impair outstanding rights under our ESPP. We will obtain stockholder approval of any amendment
to our ESPP as required by applicable law or listing requirements.
